newsitem.title: UK: Ice blockages boost NWE gas oil barge premiums.
newsitem.headline: Ice blockages boost NWE gas oil barge premiums.

text.p: Ice-jammed German waterways boosted NWE gas oil barge premiums on Thursday while cargoes were steady to firm on heightened demand for heating oil, traders said.
"It's hell out there. They're moving product by rail and truck instead," a trader said of the inland market in Germany, Europe's largest heating oil market.
Frigid temperatures across Europe sent benchmark Jan IPE futures up $8.25 higher to $232 a tonne at the close.
The blockages are mainly in canals serving inland Germany and waterways connecting inland Germany with the Rotterdam region.
Barges traded throughout the day in a range from Jan IPE +$1 to +$2.50, up to $2 higher than New Year's Eve. Low sulphur diesel remained dormant, with premiums around Jan IPE +$10/12.
Cargoes saw less action, with players still on leave. Traders sought an arbitrage in heating oil from the U.S. Gulf to NWE but reported difficulty in securing economic freight rates.
DIN-grade heating oil traded into Germany at Jan IPE +$5.25 cif NWE, around unchanged. Russian 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil was assessed at mean quotes +$1 cif NWE.
Traders saw substantial quantities of Russian low sulphur diesel offered but little buying interest.
